messages:
oliver: Thinking about safe in-prod profiling after last week's regression. We need concrete overhead estimates for nsys/nvprof and a proposed guardrail. Anyone run broad captures on g5x/p4 recently?

maria: I ran a few short captures on g5x earlier this week. Full nsys for 30s added ~12% to 99th for small-batch inference. File sizes were huge.

ken: 12% is unacceptable for prod. Do you have breakdown CPU vs GPU scheduling overhead? Were we doing nvtx-marked capture ranges?

maria: Breakdown: cpu sampling added ~5% CPU contention, GPU scheduling latency increase ~8%. We used NVTX markers to limit capture to request-scope but the kernel timeline still got big. I can share raw kernel counts.

ana: Can you paste the exact nsys command? We should standardize the invocation for apples-to-apples comparison.

maria: Sure, this is what I used: 

```
nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 -t cuda,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none --duration=30 --force-overwrite
```

Also collected perfetto on the host side for context.

profiler-bot: NOTE: Large captures (>20s, full trace) often exceed 1GB and slow down control-plane upload. Auto-archive policy may trigger.

oliver: High-level ask: define a "surgical probe" default that is safe for hosted infra. Goals: measurable overhead <5% on 99th, bounded artifact sizes, and automatic abort/backoff. Proposal below.

oliver: Proposal v1: default sampling_rate = 0.1% of requests, capture_window = up to 1s per sample, max_captures_per_node_per_minute = 3, adaptive backoff when observed 95th latency increases >5% vs baseline.

ken: 0.1% sounds reasonable as a starting point. For large-batch workloads 1s can capture many tokens/kernels — add a tokens-per-capture cap (e.g., 2048 tokens) too.

ana: Also propose a "light" capture mode that collects kernel timestamps only (no full stream buffers). That reduces size/overhead significantly. Pseudo-flag: `--trace=config=light` or `nsys --light`.

maria: My measurements: light mode 1s -> ~2% tail impact, artifacts ~120MB. Full-mode 1s -> ~10-12% tail impact, artifacts ~400MB. So default should be light mode.

devops-bot: Ops suggestion: only run on nodes with GPU util <50% and uptime >1h to avoid noisy preemption/warmup artifacts. Also limit captures on Dedicated clusters unless explicitly allowed.

oliver: Good. We should also implement an in-proc nonblocking watchdog: if profiler overhead estimation crosses threshold mid-capture, abort capture and flag node for investigation. Telemetry: `profiler.impact_estimate` per capture.

ken: I'll draft the runtime flags: `runtime.profiler.sampling_rate` (float), `profiler.capture_window_ms` (int), `profiler.max_captures_per_minute` (int), `profiler.tokens_per_capture_cap` (int), `profiler.backoff_threshold_pct` (int), `profiler.mode` (light|full).

ana: Add `profiler.allowed_node_predicate` to only enable on nodes matching ops criteria (util/have-ssd/etc). Also add `profiler.dry_run=true` option to validate config without persisting artifacts.

maria: Uploaded CSVs and kernel counts to gs://redwood-prof/prof_runs/2034567000_metrics.csv and perfetto traces to gs://redwood-prof/perfetto/2034567000/ (link posted in channel). Raw numbers will help set better defaults.

oliver: Action list: 1) maria shares clean CSVs and summary (ETA today), 2) ken + ana open PR with runtime flags + light-mode implementation (ETA Fri), 3) add telemetry event `profiler.capture_result` and abort metrics, 4) ops will add node predicate rules.

ken: I'll also put a short playbook snippet in the PR describing safe rollout: enable in staging for 48h, run canary on 1% traffic, monitor `latency.95` and `profiler.impact_estimate`, then roll to prod with same guardrails.

ana: Quick example config we can use in PR (pseudo):

```json
{
  "runtime.profiler.sampling_rate": 0.001,
  "profiler.capture_window_ms": 1000,
  "profiler.max_captures_per_minute": 3,
  "profiler.mode": "light",
  "profiler.backoff_threshold_pct": 5
}
```

oliver: One more: implement token cap enforcement in runtime to truncate capture when token limit reached, to keep artifact sizes bounded. Also record `profiler.truncated` boolean.

maria: FYI: in my test infra I saw that enabling nvtx-range-only but forgetting to flip light-mode still produced big files. We'll add a lint check in the capture client to ensure mode=light for default policy.

devops-bot: Ops will add a Kubernetes node-label predicate `profiler=allowed` and a cluster-level rate limiter to prevent cluster-wide storms.

oliver: Thanks everyone. If ken/ana can get the PR up by EOD Friday we can run the staging rollout next week. :thumbsup:

profiler-bot: Reminder: when toggling in prod, use `--dry-run` first to validate config and ensure `profiler.impact_estimate` stays below threshold before enabling artifact persistence.

oliver: noted, wrapping up.
